title: The Border of Vienna
premise: Marguerite Winterbourne, a financial-crimes investigator who testified against the Voss Syndicate and vanished into witness protection, is living a hollow half-life of laundered normalcy when a real-estate listing exposes his safe house — interior photos, his furniture, his life for sale. The listing is a message: someone inside the protection program has sold him out, and the defector he's ordered to extract from Vienna, a Voss accountant named Ilse Brandt, may be the bait in a trap designed to flush him out. As Marguerite races across a city of shadows and shell companies, he must decide whether survival is worth becoming the kind of man he once hunted. In the end, he turns the trap inside out — sacrificing his anonymity forever to deliver the evidence that destroys the Syndicate's protector within the program itself.
about_author: Felix Montrose is the pen name of a former compliance officer who spent a decade tracing money through Eastern European banks before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers from an undisclosed European city, drawing on the gray zones where finance and espionage quietly overlap.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Scrolling property sites at 3 a.m., he finds his own safe house listed with photos of its interior — his books, his coffee cup on the counter. Panic curdles into cold clarity: only someone with access could have taken these. Emotional beat: the illusion of safety shatters.

chapters.title: Clean Money, Dirty Sleep
chapters.summary: Flashback-laced chapter establishing his old life prosecuting the Voss Syndicate and 'the incident' that killed his partner. His handler, Reyes, dismisses the listing as a glitch. Marguerite notices the photos were taken while he slept. Beat: dread deepening into paranoia.

chapters.title: The Defector File
chapters.summary: Reyes assigns him one last job: extract Ilse Brandt, a Voss accountant hiding in Vienna who wants to trade ledgers for asylum. Marguerite spots anomalies — the extraction order was routed through channels that shouldn't know he exists. Beat: reluctant duty tinged with suspicion.

chapters.title: Arrival in Gray Weather
chapters.summary: Vienna, rain on the Danube Canal. Marguerite uses dead-drop tradecraft to contact Ilse, who is sharper and more frightened than her file suggested. She tells him she never requested extraction — the request came from Vienna, in her name. Beat: the ground tilts.

chapters.title: Shell Games
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She explains the ledger structure: a Viennese private bank laundering Voss money, protected by someone codenamed GARDENER inside the witness program. Marguerite realizes the extraction order itself may be the leak. Beat: hunter and quarry become allies.

chapters.title: The Coffeehouse Dead Drop
chapters.summary: A meet with a local fixer, Tomas, at Café Sperl goes wrong when a surveillance team arrives too quickly. Marguerite and Ilse escape through service alleys; Tomas vanishes. Someone fed the location to Voss muscle. Beat: trust becomes a liability.

chapters.title: What the Photos Knew
chapters.summary: Marguerite analyzes the real-estate listing metadata: uploaded from a government VPN subnet. Only three people had access — Reyes among them. He can't tell if he's being protected, tested, or sold. Beat: isolation, the horror of doubting your only anchor.

chapters.title: The Bank on Ringstrasse
chapters.summary: Posing as an auditor, Marguerite penetrates the private bank and finds Ilse's ledger fragments — including payments to a program security contractor. A guard recognizes his face from a circulated photo. Beat: the net tightening, adrenaline and guilt.

chapters.title: Safe House, Unsafe World
chapters.summary: Holed up in a rented flat, Ilse reveals the incident's truth: his partner wasn't killed by Voss — he was killed by the program's own mole, and Marguerite's testimony was redirected to protect him. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Reyes Calls
chapters.summary: An encrypted call: Reyes orders him to abandon Ilse and come home immediately, claiming the extraction was compromised. Marguerite hears what's underneath — not concern, but fear of what Ilse knows. Beat: the moment loyalty breaks.

chapters.title: GARDENER
chapters.summary: Following the contractor payments, they identify GARDENER: Deputy Director Halloran, the man who built the witness program and now sells its secrets. Ilse's ledger has the final transaction — but it's incomplete without a physical key she left in a Vienna deposit box. Beat: a target acquires a shape.

chapters.title: The Bait Confirmed
chapters.summary: Marguerite admits the truth aloud: Ilse was never meant to be extracted — she was the lure to draw him out of hiding so both witnesses could be erased. Instead of retreating, he decides to walk into the trap deliberately. Beat: acceptance of risk, dark courage.

chapters.title: Deposit Box 114
chapters.summary: A tense retrieval at the bank vault, timed between guard rotations. Inside the box: a hardware token holding the complete ledger plus proof of Halloran's payments. They're spotted leaving; a chase through the U-Bahn ends with Marguerite wounded. Beat: cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Triage and Truth
chapters.summary: Ilse patches his shoulder in a laundromat basement. They exchange histories — two people who traded their names for safety and got neither. She confesses she once laundered money willingly; he confesses he froze during the incident. Beat: mutual absolution.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Halloran contacts Marguerite directly: return the token, and he reenters the program with a new identity, wealth, a clean slate. It's everything he's been starving for. He asks for twelve hours to decide. Beat: temptation rendered almost reasonable.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours
chapters.summary: Marguerite walks Vienna at night, weighing the offer against the man he used to be. He drafts two messages — acceptance and refusal — and burns neither. A near-miss with Voss enforcers reminds him the offer's mercy is fictional. Beat: the self reckoning with itself.

chapters.title: Counter-Trap
chapters.summary: He agrees to Halloran's meet but rigs it: copies of the ledger are already queued to three journalists, timed unless he cancels. He feeds Halloran a false location through the compromised channel, poisoning the well. Beat: the hunted becomes the architect.

chapters.title: The Meet at Schönbrunn
chapters.summary: Dusk in the palace gardens. Halloran arrives with handlers; Marguerite arrives with nothing but the truth and a recorder. Halloran's men close in — then federal prosecutors, tipped via the journalists' deadline mechanics, step out of the hedges. Beat: the trap springs inward.

chapters.title: Halloran's Fall
chapters.summary: Confrontation: Halloran argues he kept the program alive by feeding it sacrifices — Marguerite included. Arrested, he still smiles, because Voss will retaliate. Marguerite realizes capture isn't the end of danger, only of pretense. Beat: victory shadowed by consequence.

chapters.title: Retribution's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: Voss enforcers hunt the pair through the city's last night of chaos. Ilse's knowledge of the Syndicate's routes saves them; a final escape across the border by night train, pursued to the last platform. Beat: exhaustion, survival purchased dearly.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Marguerite testifies openly — no glass, no alias, his name entered into the record for the first time in years. Ilse watches from the gallery. The Syndicate's finances unravel publicly. Beat: reclaiming identity as an act of power.

chapters.title: The Border of Vienna
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Marguerite sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident, in a small flat he chose himself. The safe house sells to strangers; he hopes they never learn what it held. Some borders you cross; some you finally stop guarding. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
